skill.name: video-inpainting
skill.description: Region edits across video frames on RunComfy via the `runcomfy` CLI — remove an object that appears across many frames, clean up wires or watermarks, replace a region with matching motion. Routes across Wan 2-7 edit-video (default, prompt-driven region edits with spatial language), Lucy Edit Restyle (identity-stable region-aware restyle), and Seedream 4-0 edit-sequential (when treating the clip as a frame stack). Picks the right route based on whether the change is prose-driven, identity-locked, or needs frame-by-frame still inpaint chained into a video. Triggers on "video inpaint", "video inpainting", "remove from video", "mask region in video", "clean up video", "remove object from clip", "video patch", "frame-by-frame edit", "remove watermark from video", "remove passing person", or any explicit ask to edit a region across video frames.
skill.summary: Guide regional video edits through RunComfy models, with workflow recommendations for precise masking.
skill.author: prime-skills

security_audit.summary: All 57 static findings are false positives involving Markdown, reference URLs, standard authentication documentation, or model-selection advice. One semantic concern remains: the guide incorrectly treats JSON input as protection against shell injection during command construction. No evidence found of malicious instructions, credential exfiltration, or security-review manipulation; external CLI behavior was not verified.

remediation.issue: The shell-safety guarantee omits quoting requirements for user-provided prompts and URLs.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the absolute guarantee and document structured JSON serialization with argument-array execution or supported file input, without interpolating untrusted text into shell commands.

semantic_findings.title: Shell Safety Claim Omits Caller-Side Quoting
semantic_findings.description: The guide claims "No shell-injection surface" while placing user prompts and URLs inside shell-single-quoted JSON. An unescaped apostrophe can end that quoting before the CLI receives input; JSON does not protect the invoking shell.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The example and absolute safety claim are visible, but no CLI implementation or dynamically assembled command is included. Exploitability depends on how an agent inserts user input.

content.value_statement: Unwanted objects and inconsistent regions can distract viewers across an entire video. This skill guides RunComfy model selection and regional editing prompts while identifying tasks that require separate masking workflows.
actual_capabilities: Recommends Wan, Lucy, or Seedream routes based on regional edit intent, identity preservation, and frame-sequence requirements.
Provides a RunComfy CLI example for submitting a source video URL and an edit prompt to Wan.
Guides spatial targeting, preservation instructions, and separate passes for individual edits.
Identifies ComfyUI workflows for pixel-precise masks and temporal propagation outside the CLI.
Explains CLI authentication, output-directory selection, and common exit codes.
limitations: Requires an external RunComfy CLI installation, authentication, network access, and access to the selected service model.
Prompt-driven edits do not guarantee pixel-precise targeting or unchanged surrounding content.
Mask propagation requires separate GUI workflows; frame extraction and video re-encoding require separate tools.
This package contains guidance only; external CLI security claims and model performance were not verified.

output_examples.input: Can I edit every frame independently and rebuild a long video?
output: Seedream sequential editing is suggested for short frame sequences.
Independent still edits can lose temporal consistency on long clips.
Frame extraction and video re-encoding require separate tools.

best_practices: Use source URLs explicitly provided for the task, and confirm authorization before sharing footage with an external service.
Describe one spatially specific change per pass, request preservation, and inspect motion continuity after each edit.
Serialize inputs and use argument-array execution where available; do not interpolate prompts or URLs directly into shell commands.
anti_patterns: Combining unrelated regional edits into one prompt and expecting unchanged surrounding frames.
Treating prompt-driven endpoints as substitutes for precise masks or guaranteed temporal propagation.
Assuming JSON prevents shell injection or treating unverified CLI privacy claims as established guarantees.

faq.question: What must I install before using this skill?
faq.answer: The guide requires the RunComfy CLI and a signed-in account. Network access and access to the selected model are also required.

faq.question: Which model is the default?
faq.answer: Wan 2-7 Edit-Video is the default for prompt-driven regional edits. Lucy and Seedream are alternatives for specific editing requirements.

faq.question: Can the CLI propagate exact masks?
faq.answer: Not through the documented endpoints. The guide directs precise masking and temporal propagation tasks to separate ComfyUI GUI workflows.

faq.question: Will all other content remain unchanged?
faq.answer: No guarantee is provided. Explicit preservation prompts and one change per pass can reduce drift, but every result requires visual review.

faq.question: Does this skill process video locally?
faq.answer: No local video-processing engine is included. The documented CLI sends requests to RunComfy, polls job status, and downloads results.

faq.question: Is JSON input sufficient protection against shell injection?
faq.answer: No. JSON structures the model request but does not escape the invoking shell. Use structured serialization and safe argument passing for user input.
